Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Nimbus Health is ready to move forward with a 4-week POC to validate Redwood for our clinical documentation summarization and user-facing search. The exec team has asked for a crisp list of acceptance criteria and exit gates so they can sign off internally.

Top priorities from our side:
- Accuracy of clinical entity extraction (precision >= 0.88 on our sample set)
- Summaries in clinician style (average human eval score >= 4/5)
- End-to-end 95th percentile latency < 350ms for 512-token requests
- No PHI persist beyond session (we need confirmation of retention policy)

Can you send over a MAP that includes: target acceptance tests, who owns each test, dates, and the formal exit gate definitions? Also flag anything that would block our security/compliance review so we can loop in InfoSec.

Appreciate a one-page checklist we can show the execs.

Best,
Elena

Summary (POC window: Mar 9 - Apr 2):
- Acceptance tests: accuracy (entity extraction), summary quality (human eval rubric), latency & throughput (95p token timing), security (data retention, KMS handling).
- Exit gates (examples):
  - AC1 (Accuracy): >=0.88 precision on 500-sample closed set across 3 clinical domains.
  - AC2 (Quality): mean rater score >=4.0 on 50 clinician-blinded summaries.
  - AC3 (Perf): 95th percentile latency <350ms at target concurrency of 8 RPS.
  - AC4 (Security): SOC2 controls documented + contract timeline for retention settings.
- Owners: Redwood (neha_kapoor for test harness + infra, vanessa for program coordination), Nimbus (Elena/Samir for sample data and clinical raters).
- Go/no-go: go if AC1-AC4 met OR if only minor deviations (documented and approved) — details in the MAP.

Neha — can you add the technical test plan (load test harness, data redaction steps, and evaluation rubric) and a short checklist for the security docs we should provide?

I will convert the MAP into a one-page executive checklist for your team and push an updated version by EOD Friday. Also adding our HubSpot milestone link to the MAP for transparency: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9843.

Hi all — drafting the technical acceptance tests and some practical exit gate definitions. Attaching a short test plan (poc_test_plan.md) that we will use to run the evaluation. Key items: 

1) Data & test harness
- Nimbus provides a 500-record de-identified sample set (3 domains). Redwood will run through our scoring pipeline and return token-level deltas.
- Test harness details: seed, deterministic sampling, and evaluation scripts are in poc_test_plan.md.

2) Accuracy (AC1)
- Metric: precision@entity (clinical entity extraction) on holdout set. Threshold: >=0.88.
- Measurement: automated script + manual spot-check of 50 records. Failure mode: <0.82 -> automatic fail; 0.82-0.88 -> requires joint remediation plan.

3) Quality (AC2)
- Human rater protocol: 5 clinician raters, blinded. Rubric scores 1-5. Mean >=4.0 required. If mean between 3.5-4.0, require targeted prompt/parameter tuning and re-run.

4) Performance (AC3)
- Load: 8 RPS sustained, burst to 20 RPS.
- Latency target: 95th <350ms for 512-token. If 95th between 350-500ms, allow one remediation sprint; >500ms is fail.

5) Security / retention (AC4)
- Redwood confirms session-only KV caching by default; retention false unless explicitly enabled. Need to provide configuration snippet and KMS flow for keys.
- Deliverable: SOC2 extract + data flow diagram. If any redlines in DocuSign or retention policy not acceptable, that's an exit gate pause.

Timeline proposal (conservative):
- Mar 9: Redwood infra ready + test harness validated
- Mar 10-20: run automated tests & collect candidate summaries
- Mar 21-26: clinician blind rating and scoring
- Mar 29: joint review of results; decision meeting Apr 1

I'll maintain the harness in the shared GSheet and post the scripts once sandbox is provisioned.

Attachments: poc_test_plan.md (test harness, scripts, and evaluation rubric).

- Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
